step2.title: Complete the Road
step2.description: The road is still under construction. It takes time to actually begin and complete. Let's advance time and wait for it. Press the "Start" button on the toolbar to progress time. Construction incurs monthly costs while underway.

step3.title: Create a Parcel
step3.description: The road is complete! Now let's create a parcel to build on. Select the parcel icon from the toolbar.
step3.create: Make sure "Create Along Road" is selected, then click the road in the 3D view. When you see red outlines along the road, press confirm to create the parcels.

step4.title: Build a Building
step4.description: Now you can build! Select the building icon from the toolbar.
step4.select: Choose "Apartment" from the "Residential" category. Pick any of the parcels you just created as the construction site, then press confirm to build.

step5.title: Complete the Building
step5.description: Like roads, buildings don't complete instantly. It's still under construction, so advance time and wait for it to finish.

controls.title: Basic Controls
controls.description: Learn the cockpit, the display panel and the icon panel, how epochs advance time, how to move the camera, and where the city boundary is.

step1.title: Look at the cockpit
step1.tools: Let's look at the cockpit. The highlighted buttons are the everyday tools. "View" opens the display panel and "Map" opens a map of the whole city. "Bulldozer" is a mode that removes empty parcels and planned buildings and roads, and "Drive" lets you travel through the city and look around. When you've read this, press "Next".
step1.services: This is the public service gauge. It shows whether supply capacity is keeping up with demand. Demand grows as the city grows, so check it from time to time. Press "Next".
step1.status: "Score" is your governance score (per household, out of 2.0). "Budget" shows the expected budget for this period and your cash on hand. Press "Next".
step1.notifications: Events in the city arrive at the "Notifications" button. The date and weather are shown here too. That's the cockpit. Press "Next".

step2.title: Open the display panel
step2.open: Press "View" in the cockpit to open the display panel.
step2.tabs: The vertical tabs are display layers. Use them to switch what you want to look at. Press "Next".
step2.modes: Each tab has buttons that switch how it is displayed. Use them when you want to see the state of the city in a particular way. Leave the panel open and press "Next".

step3.title: Look at the icon panel
step3.road: Let's go through the icon panel one icon at a time. "Roads, Rail & Infrastructure" lays roads, tracks, power lines, water pipes and other paths. Press "Next" to move on to the next icon.
step3.land: "Land Parcels" creates the parcels on which buildings are built.
step3.grading: "Earthworks" adjusts the ground height to create flat land and reclaimed land.
step3.district: "District" groups parcels into districts and restricts which kinds of buildings can be built.
step3.construction: "Construction" is where you plan homes, shops, factories, public facilities and other buildings.
step3.constructionProjects: "Construction Projects" lists planned and ongoing works, grouped by tag.
step3.transport: "Public Transport" creates and manages bus, rail and other lines.
step3.regulation: "Regulations" sets speed limits, the initial building regulations for new districts, immigration conditions, social security and repair settings.
step3.city: "Policies" sets taxes such as income tax, business tax and consumption tax.
step3.finance: "Financial Policy" sets quantitative easing and shows the financial state: money supply, GDP, prices and more.
step3.stat: "Statistics" shows statistics such as population and commuting as charts.
step3.propPlacement: "Prop Placement" places scenic props (small objects) on the terrain. That's the end of the icon panel. Press "Next".

step4.title: Advance time with epochs
step4.flow: Time in this game advances in units called epochs. Before each epoch, you allocate the budget and make construction plans. When your plans are ready, press "Start" to run the simulation.
step4.execute: The city does not change until you press "Start", so you can take your time planning. The city moves only while an epoch runs, and the results are shown when it ends. You don't need to press it now; when you've finished reading, press "Next".

step5.title: Move the camera
step5.description: You can move the camera like this: drag with the left button to move the view, drag with the right button to rotate, W/A/S/D (or the arrow keys) to move, Q/E to rotate, R/F to change the height, and the mouse wheel to zoom. Try it freely, then press "Next".

step6.title: Fly mode and cinema mode
step6.description: The camera has two special modes. "Fly mode" starts with Shift+F: move along your view with W/A/S/D, look around with the mouse, and go up or down with R/F. Press Esc to leave it. "Cinema mode" starts from the button in the top-right corner of the screen and lets you circle around the city. Look around with the mouse; Shift switches between orbiting and travelling, Space pauses, Backspace reverses, and Esc exits. The on-screen panels are hidden while either mode is on and come back when you press Esc. When you've tried them, exit both modes and press "Next".

step7.title: See the city boundary
step7.description: We moved the camera to the east edge of the city. The area you can use as a city is this rectangle where detailed terrain exists, and the camera cannot leave it either. That's all for the basic controls. Press "Next" to finish the tutorial.

scenario2.title: Set Up Districts
scenario2.description: The town wants to mine an ore deposit, but other buildings could occupy the land. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to locate natural resources, divide the town into districts, and restrict which types of buildings can be built.

step1.title: Create a District
step1.description: A district is a unit that divides the city into areas, and it is assigned to each side of a road. A parcel belongs to the district on the side of the road it faces. Press the district button on the icon panel to open the Edit Districts window: you'll see that the H-shaped road network forms a single district.
step1.create: This road network has no blocks enclosed by roads, so switch the brush to "Street Side". Keeping the "New District" tool, hold Ctrl and drag along the upper-right road of the H. Both sides of the road you paint, along with the parcels facing them, become a new district.

step2.title: District Created
step2.description: You've split off part of the city as a new district. Districts let you aggregate figures such as prices and population per district, and apply building regulations to the district as a whole. Once you've checked it, close the Edit Districts window.

step3.title: Show Natural Resources
step3.description: Let's check whether this district contains natural resources. Open the display modes with the eye icon in the cockpit at the bottom center of the screen, and turn natural resources on in the natural resources tab. Once they appear, click the ore vein at the yellow marker to open its details.

step4.title: Open District Details
step4.description: You can see there's an ore vein where you created the new district. This area looks like a good spot for a mine. Click the label of the district you just created to open its detail panel.

step5.title: Set Building Regulations
step5.description: Using the building regulations near the bottom of the panel, you can choose which buildings may be built on the parcels in this district. We only want mines here, so click every building other than "Mine" to disable them.

step6.title: Check a Parcel
step6.description: You've set building regulations for the district. Let's confirm they are reflected on the parcels inside it. Click the parcel with the yellow marker to open its detail panel.

step7.title: Regulation Applied
step7.description: Looking near the bottom of the parcel panel, you can see the district's regulation allowing only "Mine" is reflected here. You can no longer build anything other than a mine on this parcel.

scenario3.title: Build the Infrastructure
scenario3.description: Residents have no electricity at home. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to build a power plant and a substation, connect them with power lines, and check that electricity reaches homes.

step1.description: The apartment building in this town doesn't have electricity yet. Click the apartment building with the yellow marker to open its details, pick one of the tenants in the "Building Info" tab, then open its "Trade" tab: you can see that the Acquired amount of Electricity is 0.
step1.title: Check the Apartment Building

step2.description: To generate electricity, you need a power plant. Build a "Solar Power Plant" on the parcel with the yellow marker on the flat land west of town. It would normally take time to complete, but since this is a tutorial, the construction period is skipped once confirmed and the plant is completed.
step2.title: Build a Solar Power Plant

step3.description: The high-voltage electricity produced by a power plant can't be used by households as it is. Build a "Substation" on the parcel with the yellow marker next to the apartment building to convert it into power that homes can use. A substation's electricity reaches a certain area around it.
step3.title: Build a Substation

step4.description: Open "Roads, Rail & Infrastructure" on the icon panel and choose "Power Line" under "Electricity". Draw a line from the solar power plant's connection terminal to the substation's terminal in town. Even though they're far apart, a straight line between the terminals does it in one go. Once confirmed, the power line is completed and the connection is checked.
step4.title: Connect with a Power Line

step5.description: Advance epochs and check whether the substation is receiving high-voltage electricity. Click the substation to open its details and, in the "Trade" tab, make sure the Received amount of High-voltage electricity isn't 0. It takes a few epochs for the power plant to start up and the power to arrive.
step5.title: Confirm the Power Supply

step6.description: Finally, open a tenant's "Trade" tab from the apartment building's details as in step 1, and check that the Acquired amount of Electricity is no longer 0. It may take a few more epochs for power to reach households. Generation, transmission and transformation linked together bring power to homes — that's how power infrastructure works, and water supply works the same way.
step6.title: Infrastructure Complete

step9.title: Shape the curved climbing branch
step9.description: Choose Railway track. Start at the depot’s eastern ground-level terminal, make a broad loop east through the intermediate markers, and join the main line at 6m. Use the Ctrl settings menu to select curves. PageUp/1 raises height; PageDown/2 lowers it. Spread the rise gradually over a long route, roughly 0→1→2→3→4→5→6m. Right-click to finish the shape, then drag vertices and control handles to smooth it. Approach the east-west main line at a shallow angle. Widen a curve if its radius falls below 100m; lengthen the climb or spread the height changes if the grade exceeds 5%. Remove red violations before confirming. Next completes the track and checks alignment and connection.

complete.title: Tutorial Complete
complete.description: Congratulations! You have completed the tutorial. Press "Finish" to close the guide and keep playing this city freely.

tutorial.failed: Condition not met. Please try again.

guide.openRoad: Open the construction panel using the road icon.
guide.selectRoad: Select the ground-level two-lane street. Only the required variant is available.
guide.placeStart: Left-click inside the cyan circle to place the start of the road.
guide.placeEnd: Left-click inside the yellow circle to place the end of the road.
guide.finalizeRoad: Right-click in the 3D view to finish the road shape.
guide.confirmRoad: Confirm in the construction panel to save the road, then press "Next".
guide.failed: Setup or communication failed. Retry; if the problem persists, exit and start the tutorial in a new city.
guide.placementRequired: Use the variant and positions shown by the guide.
guide.finishFailed: Could not finish the tutorial. Please try again.

trade.title: Start international trade
trade.description: A local factory wants to reach overseas customers. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to export food through a port and import goods by freight rail from a neighboring country.

step1.description: Build a "Container Terminal" on the coastal parcel with the yellow marker. Once confirmed, the construction period is skipped.
step1.title: Build a container port

step2.description: Advance epochs and check the food exports in the port's details. It takes a few epochs for the factory's production and transport to get going.
step2.title: Confirm food exports

step3.description: Build an "International Freight Station" on the parcel with the yellow marker along the road. At the eastern border, there is a railway leading into the neighboring country and a border freight station.
step3.title: Build an international freight station

step4.open: Open "Roads, Rail & Infrastructure" on the icon panel and choose "Container Freight Platform" under "Railways".
step4.place: Lay a platform north of the international freight station, parallel to it. Left-click inside the cyan circle (west) to place the start and inside the yellow circle (east) to place the end, then right-click in the 3D view to finish the shape. Switch "Platform Side" to "Inside" and check that the platform is on the station building's side (the south side) before confirming. When you're done, press "Next".
step4.title: Build a platform beside the station

step5.description: Press "Back" to return to the list, choose "Railway Track", and lay track from the east end of the platform to the west end of the border freight station's platform. Once confirmed, the track is completed and the connection is checked.
step5.title: Lay track to the border

step6.title: Build a Depot
step6.description: Build a "Rail Depot" on the parcel with the yellow marker along the road. Press "Next" and, since this is a tutorial, the construction period is skipped.

step7.title: Connect the Depot to the Main Line
step7.description: Lay a siding from the connection terminal on the north side of the depot to the main line. Join the main line at a shallow angle heading east rather than at a right angle. When you're done, press "Next".

step8.description: Open "Roads, Rail & Infrastructure" on the icon panel and use "Power Line" under "Electricity" to connect the connection terminal of the solar power plant east of town to the depot's connection terminal.
step8.title: Supply power to the depot

step9.description: In "Public Transport", press "+ New line" and choose "International Freight Line" as the line type. Place stops on the platforms of the international freight station and the border freight station, and open the line. Trains cannot pass each other on single track, so set the target headway to 45 minutes so that one train can make the round trip. Once confirmed, the city's import gateway switches from the port to the international freight station.
step9.title: Open the international freight line

step10.description: Advance epochs and check the imports in the international freight station's details. Procuring vehicles and getting transport up and running takes a few epochs.
step10.title: Confirm rail imports

highway.title: Build a motorway
highway.description: The town needs another route for vehicles as it grows. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to build an elevated highway over a local road and connect them with ramps to create an interchange.

step1.title: Cross above the street
step1.open: Cross the central street with an elevated motorway. Open "Roads, Rail & Infrastructure" on the icon panel and choose the two-lane motorway under "Motorways".
step1.start: Left-click inside the cyan circle to place the start of the motorway. It snaps to a viaduct 7 m above the ground.
step1.end: Left-click inside the yellow circle to place the end. It snaps to the same 7 m height on the far side of the street.
step1.confirm: Confirm in the construction panel to save the motorway, then press "Next". Since this is a tutorial, construction time is skipped and it is completed right away.

step2.title: Name the motorway
step2.description: Register the new motorway as a named road and enter its name in the details panel.

step3.title: Build a ramp
step3.description: Connect the elevated motorway to the central street with a ramp. Confirmation completes construction and checks for an interchange.

step4.title: Inspect the interchange
step4.description: Open the interchange details and confirm the connection between the street and motorway.

mining.title: Mine resources
mining.description: Valuable resources lie beneath the island, but there's no way to haul them out. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to set up a mine, freight railway, and port to extract ore, transport it, and export it overseas.

step1.description: Enable natural resources and inspect the marked southeastern ore deposit in MineCity2.
step1.title: Inspect the ore vein

step2.description: Build a Mine on the marked ore plot. Next skips construction time.
step2.title: Build a mine

step3.description: Build an Ore loading station on the large existing plot southeast of the mine. Its platform belongs on the southwest side.
step3.title: Build a loading station next to the mine

step4.description: Build an Ore unloading station on the existing plot south of the harbor road.
step4.title: Build an unloading station near the port

step5.description: Build a Bulk port on the marked coastal plot.
step5.title: Build a bulk port

step6.open: Choose Ore freight platform and connect each pair of markers southwest of the loading station and south of the unloading station. Face the platforms toward their facilities.
step6.loading: Choose Ore freight platform and connect each pair of markers southwest of the loading station and south of the unloading station. Face the platforms toward their facilities.
step6.unloading: Choose Ore freight platform and connect each pair of markers southwest of the loading station and south of the unloading station. Face the platforms toward their facilities.
step6.title: Build platforms beside the stations

step7.town: The stations are not yet connected. Lay freight track from the eastern harbor-platform end, past the intermediate road bend, to the northwestern mountain-platform end. Use smooth curves; choose Non-following terrain for the climb and adjust grade and radius until red violations disappear. Add intermediate points so each span remains below 500m.
step7.climb: The stations are not yet connected. Lay freight track from the eastern harbor-platform end, past the intermediate road bend, to the northwestern mountain-platform end. Use smooth curves; choose Non-following terrain for the climb and adjust grade and radius until red violations disappear. Add intermediate points so each span remains below 500m.
step7.title: Connect the two stations by rail

step8.title: Build a Depot
step8.description: Build a Rail depot on the existing plot southwest of the harbor, with its connection terminal at the eastern end.

step9.title: Connect the Depot to the Main Line
step9.description: Connect the depot’s eastern terminal to the western harbor-platform end with a smooth shallow-angle branch.

step10.description: Connect the existing solar plant terminal to the depot’s eastern shared terminal with a power line.
step10.title: Supply power to the depot

step11.description: Create an Ore transport line, place stops on both ore freight platforms, and click the first stop to close the return loop. Trains cannot pass each other on single track, so set the target headway to 45 minutes so that one train can make the round trip, then confirm.
step11.title: Open the ore freight line

step12.description: Run epochs to get mining, loading, rail transport, unloading, and exports going. Procuring vehicles and getting transport up and running takes a few epochs.
step12.title: Advance epochs

step13.description: Advance epochs and inspect the coastal Bulk port’s ore receipts and exports. Mining, vehicle procurement and transport take several epochs.
step13.title: Confirm ore exports

tourism.title: Develop tourism
tourism.description: The island needs a harbor, accommodation, and a bus route to welcome visitors to its ruins. Learn to build a hotel and passenger terminal, create a bus route, and check tourist arrivals, restaurant sales, and bus use.

step1.description: Build a Tourist Hotel on the lot marked in yellow west of the ancient ruins. Construction time is skipped when you confirm.
step1.title: Build a hotel beside the ruins

step2.description: Build a Passenger Terminal on the marked harbor lot. A bus depot is ready, but there are no bus routes yet.
step2.title: Build a passenger terminal

step3.description: Open Public Transport → New line and choose Bus Route. Place stops on the roads at the yellow markers in this order: harbor → housing → ruins → housing. Click the first harbor stop to close the return loop. Set the fare to 0 and the target headway to 1 minute, then confirm.
step3.title: Create a bus route from the harbor to the ruins

step4.description: Advance epochs to welcome tourists. Facilities and bus vehicle procurement take a few epochs to get going.
step4.title: Advance the epoch

step5.description: Check the restaurant by the ruins and the bus route you created. Complete this step when tourists have arrived, restaurant sales exceed their starting level, and the bus has passengers. Advance more epochs if needed.
step5.title: Check restaurant sales and bus passengers

intro.basic: People are hoping to start a new life in this town, but there aren't enough homes to welcome them. In this tutorial, you'll learn the full process of planning roads and buildings, advancing time, and seeing construction through to completion.
intro.controls: You have just taken office as mayor, and a wide stretch of land lies ahead of you. Before you start building, it helps to know how to read the screen and how to operate the basics. In this tutorial, you'll learn what the cockpit and the icon panel do, how epochs advance time, how to move the camera, and where the city boundary is.
intro.scenario2: An ore deposit has been found in a corner of town. Unless the land is protected, other buildings could go up on top of it. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to locate natural resources, divide the town into districts, and restrict which types of buildings can be built.
intro.scenario3: The people of this town live in homes without electricity. They want to turn on lights and use appliances, but the facilities to generate power and deliver it to their homes are missing. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to build a power plant and a substation, connect them with power lines, and check that electricity reaches homes.
intro.scenario4: MetroCity needs a railway, but private buildings and a public hospital obstruct its route. In this tutorial you will learn land acquisition, explicit public demolition, elevated track above roads, platforms and stations, a depot, curve and grade adjustment, power connection and opening a service.
intro.trade: A local food factory has asked for help selling its products overseas. The town also wants a way to bring in goods it needs from abroad. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to export food through a port and import goods by freight rail from a neighboring country.
intro.highway: As the town grows, more vehicles will carry people and goods through it. The town wants another route ready so through traffic won't all end up on the local road. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to build an elevated highway over a local road and connect them with ramps to create an interchange.
intro.mining: Valuable resources lie beneath this island, but there is no way to haul them from the mountain to the port. Without transport, the island can't turn that wealth into an industry. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to set up a mine, freight railway, and port to extract ore, transport it, and export it overseas.
intro.tourism: The islanders want to share their ancient seaside ruins with more visitors. But they lack a passenger harbor, accommodation, and a bus route from the harbor to town. In this tutorial, you will learn to build a hotel and passenger terminal, create a bus route, and check tourist arrivals, restaurant sales, and bus use.
intro.heading: A Request for the Mayor
intro.reclamation: This tiny reef has no flat ground for a city hall. In this tutorial, you will learn to reclaim coastal land, create a parcel, and place a city hall.
intro.acquisition: Homes, offices, and a fire station stand between two elevated platforms. In this tutorial, you will learn to plan tracks, acquire private land, explicitly demolish a public facility, and complete the connection.

reclamation.title: Reclaim the coast
reclamation.description: This tiny reef has no flat ground for a city hall. In this tutorial, you will learn to reclaim coastal land, create a parcel, and place a city hall.

step1.title: Plan the reclamation
step1.description: Open the grading tool. Left-click the four yellow markers in order to draw a rectangle from the shore into the sea. Right-click to close it, check that the estimate is for reclamation, and confirm the project.

step2.title: Complete the reclaimed land
step2.description: Use Start to advance at least one epoch, then press Next. Since this lesson has no construction suppliers, Next skips the remaining reclamation work. The sea inside the project becomes land.

step3.title: Create a parcel on the new land
step3.description: Open the parcel tool and choose Single. Set both Depth and Length to 60 m, click the center of the four markers, and confirm. Keep the parcel inside the reclaimed land, away from the quay, with enough room for a city hall.

step4.title: Place the city hall
step4.description: Open the building tool, select City Hall in the Public Services category, and place it at the center of your new parcel. Placing it founds the city and completes this tutorial.

acquisition.title: Land acquisition and metro construction
acquisition.description: Homes, offices, and a fire station stand between two elevated platforms. In this tutorial, you will learn to plan tracks, acquire private land, explicitly demolish a public facility, and complete the connection.

step1.title: Connect the platforms with tracks
step1.open: Open the road and railway tool. Connect the two existing platforms with elevated tracks 7 m above the ground.
step1.start: Select Double Track and left-click the inner end of the western platform at the cyan marker. The start snaps to the existing endpoint at a height of 7 m.
step1.end: Left-click the inner end of the eastern platform at the yellow marker. You can plan construction even where the tracks overlap homes and offices.
step1.confirm: Review the estimate and press Confirm. This lesson covers track construction; it does not require setting up a train service.
step1.variant: In the railway category, select the highlighted Double Track card.

step2.title: Observe acquisition and the obstruction
step2.description: Use Start to advance an epoch. Acquisition negotiations begin for private parcels in the track corridor. The fire station at the yellow marker is a public facility, so it cannot be acquired automatically and the tracks remain planned. Inspect parcel and building details to see what is happening.

step3.title: Demolish the fire station explicitly
step3.description: Click the fire station at the yellow marker to open its details, then press Bulldoze to order its removal. Public facilities require your explicit demolition order. Leave the other homes and offices to land acquisition.

step4.title: Wait for acquisition and completion
step4.description: Keep advancing epochs with Start. Track construction proceeds once private land acquisition and demolition are complete. Connecting the two platforms with completed tracks finishes this tutorial.

tip1.title: The Epoch System
tip1.description: In this game, you can take your time to plan budgets and construction before advancing time. The city's state won't change until you click 'Run Simulation'.

tip2.title: Maintaining Public Facilities
tip2.description: Public facilities like fire and police stations degrade over time. Lacking maintenance budget reduces their efficiency, or in the worst case, causes them to collapse.

tip3.title: Road Connections & Parcels
tip3.description: Parcels belong to districts based on the road they face. Buildings cannot be constructed on unconnected parcels, preventing any economic activity.

tip4.title: Citizen Needs & QOL
tip4.description: Citizens live by consuming products like food, healthcare, and entertainment. When these are supplied sufficiently, their Quality of Life (QOL) improves.

tip5.title: Approximate Simulation
tip5.description: To keep the game running smoothly even as cities grow huge, traffic and supply/demand are calculated using approximate mathematical models instead of simulating every single car and citizen individually.

tip6.title: Build Fire Stations in the City
tip6.description: Fire stations should be near where buildings are dense. A station on the outskirts won't make it in time when it counts.

tip7.title: Slow Down on Curves
tip7.description: Set lower speed limits on roads with sharp curves. Roads that are too fast see a lot more accidents.

tip8.title: Schools Make Cities Prosper
tip8.description: Educating citizens opens the door to more advanced industries. If you want hospitals and factories, start by investing in schools.

tip9.title: Don't Forget Maintenance
tip9.description: Buildings deteriorate and can collapse if left alone. Open the budget panel and make sure your maintenance allocation isn't sitting at zero.

tip10.title: Fire Spreads
tip10.description: Fires can spread to neighboring buildings in dense areas. Spread your fire stations across different parts of the city rather than clustering them.

tip11.title: Spread Police Stations Too
tip11.description: Like fire stations, police stations lose effectiveness with distance. Build them near areas where crime is rising.

tip12.title: Use Immigration Filters
tip12.description: You can set immigration requirements in the Regulation window. Filtering by skill or age lets you attract the kind of residents your city needs.

tip13.title: Districts Help You Stay Organized
tip13.description: Grouping roads into districts lets you view stats and set regulations by area. Once your city starts growing, districts become essential.

tip14.title: Better Safe Than Sorry
tip14.description: If critical infrastructure shuts down due to accidents or disasters, the city's economy will take a massive hit. Build redundant facilities to keep backups ready.

tip15.title: Don't Let It Sprawl
tip15.description: When there are not enough parcels for the demand, roads and parcels appear on their own in a disorderly way. Develop the city deliberately to keep slums from forming.

tip16.title: Industrial Clusters
tip16.description: Productivity rises when similar industries or raw material producers are nearby. Create industrial zones and tech districts to bring businesses together.

tip17.title: Can You Work Around the Clock?
tip17.description: Longer working hours raise productivity. Entertainment spending and health take the hit.

tip18.title: Commuter Hell
tip18.description: Longer commutes mean less spending on entertainment.

tip19.title: Think Ahead
tip19.description: You cannot run trains longer than station platforms. Build your railway with room to grow.

tip20.title: Bury the Problem
tip20.description: Underground roads produce neither noise nor air pollution. Some problems really can be solved by burying them.

tip21.title: In the Shadow of Progress
tip21.description: Tall buildings cast shadows on their neighbors, making the area less pleasant to live in. Your city may have a bright future, but its streets could be in the dark.

tip22.title: Trade the Keys for a Transit Pass
tip22.description: With convenient public transit, even wealthy residents can give up their cars and spend their money on other things.

tip23.title: Now Transporting: Air
tip23.description: Even empty buses take up road space. Do not turn your congestion relief plan into a traffic jam.

tip24.title: Moles Pay No Rent
tip24.description: Tunnels below a certain depth need no land acquisition. If negotiations get tough, dig deeper.

tip25.title: The High Road to Work
tip25.description: Cable cars provide transport even on steep terrain. If public transit is hard to build, leave your citizens hanging.

tip26.title: An Electrical Traffic Jam
tip26.description: Spare generating capacity is no help if the power lines cannot carry it. Before building another power plant, check for bottlenecks along the way.

tip27.title: An Unfortunate Accident
tip27.description: A building that stands in the way of development can be blown up and passed off as an accident. Public sentiment takes a heavy hit, so buy it and demolish it properly when you can.

tip28.title: No Land? Take to the Sea
tip28.description: Running out of room on land? Build offshore oil platforms and wind turbines out at sea. Connect them to your onshore transport grid with undersea pipelines and power cables.

tip29.title: Red Light Hell
tip29.description: Every intersection adds another red light. Grid layouts packed too closely together will trap drivers at every single block, and their patience will run out long before they reach their destination.

tip30.title: Good Line of Sight
tip30.description: Radio towers cover a wider area the higher they are built and the higher the ground. Signals blocked by mountains can't be overcome by sheer willpower alone.

tip31.title: Bounty of the Sea
tip31.description: If you can't find a freshwater source, you can build a desalination plant along the coast. It does require significant power, though. Finding water leads right into finding electricity.

tip32.title: Another Form of Policing
tip32.description: Unemployment is one of the root causes of crime. Don't just build police stations—provide jobs. Before agonizing over your police budget, consider investing in employment programs.

tip33.title: Bills for the Future
tip33.description: Both buildings and roads demand ongoing maintenance once built. If you overbuild just because you have spare cash, repair bills will haunt you later. Remember, that future mayor is still you.

tip34.title: Don't Over-Pump
tip34.description: If you pump water faster than the aquifer can replenish, you'll eventually face a shortage. Adding more pumps won't create more water.

tip35.title: A Costly Blunder
tip35.description: Once built, roads and buildings cannot be moved easily. Plan carefully before breaking ground. Though an unintentionally curved road can become part of the city's charm once you get used to it.

tip36.title: Surveillance Society
tip36.description: Click on pedestrians or vehicles to add citizens to your watchlist. Take a look at the daily lives of your city's residents.

hint.buildingConstruction: Select a parcel to plan a building. It takes some time from planning to completion.
hint.parcelCreation: Hold Ctrl to pick a creation method from the radial menu, then click a target in the 3D view. Adjust the size in the panel and confirm.
hint.transitCreation: Left-click to place stops in order; click the first stop to close the loop. Drag a segment to add a waypoint, drag a point to move it, right-click to delete. For a round trip, also place the return stops.
hint.transitManagement: List of public transit lines. Adjust fares and headways, or create and delete lines. Fares affect residents' route choice. Fares that are too high reduce ridership and increase car ownership.
hint.pathConstruction: Construct roads and railways. Click on the terrain in the 3D view: left-click to add vertices, right-click to confirm the shape, and drag vertices to reposition them. Hold Ctrl to open the settings menu (curve/straight and snapping). Use 3/4 keys to change embankment/cut height.
hint.pathConstructionElevated: Construct roads and railways. Click on the terrain in the 3D view: left-click to add vertices, right-click to confirm the shape, and drag vertices to reposition them. Hold Ctrl to open the settings menu (curve/straight and snapping). Use PageUp/PageDown or 1/2 to change height, and 3/4 keys to change embankment/cut height.
hint.districtEdit: Create, expand and merge "districts", the units for regulations and statistics. Hold Ctrl in the 3D view to switch tools. Create tool: left-click a road to create a new district in the shown color (a new color is drawn each time you pick the tool). Expand tool: right-click to pick the district to grow, then left-click roads to pull them into it. Merge tool: right-click to pick the district to merge into, then left-click another district to open the confirmation panel. The selected district's color and name are shown next to the mouse cursor. Press the button again to exit.
hint.bulldozer: Bulldozer mode. Left-click to remove empty parcels, planned buildings, planned roads, and terrain props (scattered props are removed as a whole area after confirmation). Press the button again to exit.
hint.bulldozerInstant: Bulldozer mode. Left-click to instantly delete buildings, roads, empty parcels, and terrain props with no confirmation. Buildings are removed together with their tenants and residents, and terrain is not restored (the city hall, the border checkpoint, and public transit segments cannot be deleted; scattered props are still removed as a whole area after confirmation). Press the button again to exit.
hint.cityBudget: Decide how to allocate the funds earned from taxes and business operations for the next period. When the government purchases materials for road construction or public facility operations, it can only do so within the budget decided here. If the budget is insufficient, employees of public facilities may be dismissed. As a general rule, plan to use up all the cash you earn rather than saving it, and give it back to the city.
hint.resourceEdit: Create a natural resource area. Select a resource type, then click on the terrain. Left-click to add a vertex, click an edge to insert a vertex, and right-click to remove a vertex. Drag a vertex to reposition it.
hint.grading: Left-click the terrain to place vertices, then right-click to close the area. After closing, drag a vertex to move it, click an edge to add a vertex, and right-click a vertex to remove it.
